[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Technical Tutorial: Scaled Agile Framework (SAFe) Core Configurations"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"The Scaled Agile Framework (SAFe) is designed to help enterprises build better systems through agility. One of the fundamental strengths of SAFe is its flexibility, achieved through four core configurations. This tutorial provides a technical breakdown of these configurations, their components, and how to select the right setup for your enterprise architecture and delivery pipelines."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Essential SAFe"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Essential SAFe is the foundational configuration and the starting point for implementation. It is the minimal set of roles, ceremonies, and artifacts required to achieve business agility and synchronize multiple Agile teams."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Team Level: Scrum and Kanban teams building increments of value using Agile principles."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Program Level: Agile Release Train (ART) functioning as a virtual team of Agile teams (50-125 individuals)."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Key Artifacts: Program Increment (PI) Planning, System Demo, and Inspect and Adapt (I&A) events."},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Large Solution SAFe"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"Large Solution SAFe is tailored for enterprises building large-scale, complex software systems, cyber-physical systems, and enterprise solutions that do not require portfolio-level governance. It introduces the Solution Train."},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Applies to complex systems engineering where multiple ARTs must coordinate."},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Introduces roles such as Solution Train Engineer (STE), Solution Management, and Solution Architect/Engineer."},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Focuses on supplier integration, compliance, and Pre- and Post-PI Planning events."},{"order":13,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Portfolio SAFe"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"Portfolio SAFe aligns enterprise strategy with execution. It provides the governance, portfolio backlog, and funding mechanisms required to manage multiple value streams across the organization."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Strategy and Investment Funding: Connects the enterprise strategy to portfolio execution."},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Agile Portfolio Operations: Coordinates Value Streams and provides lean governance."},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Lean Governance: Manages spending through Lean Budget Guardrails and Value Stream KPIs."},{"order":18,"type":"subheading","text":"4. Full SAFe"},{"order":19,"type":"paragraph","text":"Full SAFe is the most comprehensive configuration. It includes all levels of the framework: Essential, Large Solution, and Portfolio SAFe. It is designed for large, global enterprises that develop and maintain a comprehensive portfolio of complex software and cyber-physical systems."},{"order":20,"type":"code","text":"Full SAFe Architecture Hierarchy:
[Portfolio Level] -> Strategic Themes, Lean Budgets, Portfolio Backlog
  |
  +--> [Large Solution Level] -> Solution Train, Solution Intent, Suppliers
         |
         +--> [Essential Level] -> Agile Release Train (ART), Teams, PI Planning"},{"order":21,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion and Best Practices"},{"order":22,"type":"paragraph","text":"When implementing SAFe, always start with Essential SAFe. Avoid premature scaling by jumping directly into Full SAFe. Scale up to Large Solution or Portfolio configurations only when organizational complexity demands additional coordination and governance structures."}]
